Inserting before the first statement of the exit block, without using a label-aware insertion helper, is especially consistent with the diagnostic "label ... in the middle of basic block" if the destination block begins with a label or otherwise requires splitting.

Most likely pass-level trigger/orchestrator. It is the crc pass entry point named in the issue, and it is the method that decides to call optimize_crc_loop after a chain of recognizers. Since the regression is specifically in pass crc, this method is the operational site where a misrecognized loop is transformed and no explicit CFG cleanup/verification-sensitive repair is done afterward. It is less direct than optimize_crc_loop, but it controls whether the bad transformation runs.

ranked_methods.signature: static bool gimple_find_edge_insert_loc (edge e, gimple_stmt_iterator *gsi, basic_block *new_bb)
ranked_methods.reason: High-value shared mechanism for legal statement placement relative to labels and block boundaries. Its body explicitly handles insertion after leading GIMPLE_LABELs and otherwise splits edges/blocks when necessary. That is exactly the invariant implicated by "label ... in the middle of basic block". The top candidate bypasses this infrastructure by inserting directly into a BB start, which makes this method highly relevant as the comparison point for what safe insertion should have done.

Definite surface trigger. The ICE is explicitly "verify_flow_info failed", and the issue points into this function. It is where CFG corruption is detected and escalated to internal_error. While not the upstream bug source, it is the direct failure site and therefore highly relevant for localization. Its body is generic CFG verification; the specific label-in-middle-of-BB complaint likely comes from the IL-specific verifier it calls through cfg_hooks->verify_flow_info, so this is more trigger than source.

Important precursor feeding the bad rewrite. optimize_crc_loop mutates exactly the PHI returned here, then inserts before output_crc->bb. This method assumes a single-exit loop and effectively selects the exit block/PHI target for transformation. If that exit block has nontrivial structure, including labels or only one PHI argument in a shape the pass mishandles, this method is part of the faulty setup that enables the invalid insertion/removal sequence.

Relevant contrast mechanism for safe insertion. Its purpose is to avoid illegal direct insertion in CFG-sensitive contexts by routing insertion via an edge and adjusting CFG when needed. The crc transform uses plain gsi_insert_before at the start of a basic block instead. Given the reported label-placement violation, this method strengthens the case that the bug is an unsafe insertion-site choice in the crc pass rather than a deep low-level container bug.

Low-level label/block ownership mechanism directly tied to the symptom. For GIMPLE_LABEL, it updates the label-to-block map when a label is assigned to a BB. If the crc transformation or related insertion logic causes statements to be placed before a label without corresponding structural adjustment, label-to-block ownership/invariants become relevant. Still, this is more infrastructure than likely source.

Tiny but semantically very relevant CFG primitive. The failure specifically mentions a label in the middle of a block, and this helper exists precisely to create a legal insertion point after labels. Its importance is not its size but that it represents the likely missing operation in the bad crc rewrite path.

Another safe CFG-aware insertion primitive. It inserts on an edge by first finding a valid location and creating/splitting blocks if necessary. The crc transform instead inserts directly into a block chosen from the PHI BB. Because the bug signature is illegal intra-block label placement, this method is a plausible mechanism that should have been used for structurally safe insertion.

Core block-splitting implementation that underlies legal restructuring around labels and CFG boundaries. If the crc optimization needed to materialize code at a loop-exit join point but keep labels/PHIs structurally valid, this is the sort of machinery required. It is less likely to be faulty itself than to be the operation omitted by the upstream crc transformation.
